question: Did limiting each ray's search distance to the point where it leaves the scene's outermost bounding box speed up the traversal this round?
answer: No — that optimization did not help; it made things slower and was reverted. Early in round 2 I added a pt_ray_aabb_exit helper and clamped every traversal's t_max to the distance at which the ray leaves the model-space root AABB (both the closest-hit and the shadow traversals). Measured at 512x512/64spp it came out at render_ms_best=107.004 / gpu_ms_best=106.738 with render_ms_avg=125.973, versus the pre-change state at about 101.8-103.4 best / ~110-114 avg (writer history #135-#143). The extra slab computation per ray plus the branch to install the tighter bound cost more than the pruning saved, and the average regressed notably, so I removed it entirely (#145-#151); the pt_ray_aabb_exit helper is now dead code in shaders/pt_trace.metal. What did pay off this round was a different traversal change: testing both BVH children up front and descending into the nearer one (smaller slab 'entered' distance) while pushing the other only when it is also hit — that took 93.5ms down to 64.9ms with a bit-identical PFM (#283), and combined with leaf size 1 it now sits at 59.1-66.3ms best (gpu 58.8-66.1) versus the 109.656/109.397 gate. Note the earlier measurements were taken before that near-first ordering existed, so exit pruning may behave differently on top of it, but as measured it was a clear loss and is not in the current build.

answer: No — that experiment regressed and was reverted. question: Did limiting each ray's search distance to the point where it leaves the scene's outermost bounding box speed up the traversal this round?
answer:
No — that optimization regressed and was reverted, so it contributes nothing to the current speedup.

What I tried: on the root BVH node I computed the distance at which the ray exits the model's outermost axis-aligned box and used that as the traversal's t_max instead of an open-ended / current-best t, in both the closest-hit and shadow traversals.

Measured result: render_ms_best 107.0 with render_ms_avg 126.0, versus about 101.8 best / 103.4 avg for the same build without it (writer log entries #143, #151). Both best and average got worse, so I fully reverted it; the pt_ray_aabb_exit helper it needed is still in shaders/pt_trace.metal but unused.

Why it likely hurt: the extra slab computation and the extra live value cost more per traversal step than the pruning saves. Most rays in this scene either miss the bunny entirely or hit it quickly, so the exit distance rarely tightens the bound enough to matter, while the added arithmetic and register pressure hit every step of every ray.

What actually produced this round's ~1.8x speedup (59.1-66.3ms best vs the 109.656ms gate) was the opposite kind of change: near-first child ordering in the closest-hit traversal (test both children, descend into the one with the smaller entry distance, push the other only if it is also hit) plus shrinking BVH leaves from 4 triangles to 1, with the two analytic-unit normalize() calls removed and tone mapping merged into the trace kernel. All of those were verified bit-identical against the same-seed PFM.
